draft.title: Uncertainty and error
card: a small, unpredictable variation that makes repeated readings scatter around a value. Repeating the measurement and averaging reduces its effect.
a fault that shifts every reading the same way, such as a balance that is not zeroed. Repeating and averaging does not remove it.
a range that shows how far a measured value could be from the true value, written as 12.4 ± 0.2 s. A smaller range means the result can be trusted more.
A measuring tool has a limit to its reading. A common estimate of reading uncertainty is half the smallest scale division.
draft.remember: Random error scatters readings, systematic error shifts them, and uncertainty gives the range of doubt.

a.q: A student times a trolley with a stopwatch that starts 0.3 s late every run. What type of error is this?
opts: Systematic error, as every time is shifted the same way
Random error, as the times differ from the true value
Systematic error, as the readings scatter from run to run
Random error, as averaging the times will remove it
a.why: The stopwatch shifts every reading by the same amount, so it is a systematic error. Averaging does not remove it, which is why the random error options are wrong.
a.clue: Does the fault push every reading the same way?

b.q: Mia measures a pendulum's period five times and gets 1.92, 2.05, 1.98, 2.10 and 1.95 s. Her clock is accurate. Which change best reduces the effect of the variation in her results?
opts: Repeat many more times and average the results
Subtract a fixed amount from every reading
Replace the pendulum string with a longer one
Record only the first reading to avoid confusion
b.why: The readings scatter both above and below a value, so the variation is random. Repeating and averaging reduces random error. Subtracting a fixed amount would suit a systematic shift, but the readings here are not shifted one way.
b.clue: Are the readings scattered or all shifted the same way?

a.best: Systematic error, as every time is shifted the same way

b.best: Repeat many more times and average the results
